title: Mannose-binding lectin 2 secreted by hepatocellular carcinoma cells recruits and activates natural killer cells to reshape an immune-activated microenvironment
experiments_summary:
The study employed a combination of bioinformatic analyses, in vitro cell-based assays, and in vivo animal models. Bioinformatically, high-throughput transcriptome sequencing of HCC tissues stratified by circulating tumor cell levels was integrated with the Human Secretome and Membrane Proteome database, HBV-related HCC datasets (OEP000321), ImmPort, and GSE45436 to identify MBL2 as a candidate immune regulator. TIMER was used to correlate MBL2 expression with immune cell infiltration, and Linkedomics and TCGA-LIHC datasets were queried for correlations with IFNGR1, IFNGR2, IL13R, and IL17RB. Kaplan-Meier survival analyses were conducted using TCGA-LIHC data. GEO microarray datasets and the GSE183349 dataset were used for expression and pathway correlation analyses.

For in vitro experiments, MBL2 expression was assessed across multiple HCC cell lines (Hep3B, HepG2, Huh7, MHCC97-L, MHCC97-H, LM3) by ELISA, qPCR, and western blot (WB). Stable MBL2-knockdown (shRNA) lines were generated in Huh7, and stable overexpression lines for full-length MBL2 and signal-peptide-deleted MBL2 (MBL2ΔSP) were established via lentiviral transduction in Hep3B and LM3 cells. HCC cell proliferation was evaluated by CCK-8 and colony formation assays; invasion and migration by Transwell assays. Stimulation with recombinant MBL2 (rMBL2) was used to distinguish autocrine from paracrine effects. PBMCs from 12 healthy donors were used to isolate peripheral NK cells, which were cultured with rMBL2 or PBS. NK cell activation markers (NKG2D, NKp46), degranulation (CD107a), cytotoxic proteins (GZMB, perforin), NK cell subpopulation proportions (CD56dim/CD56bright), and cytokine production (IFN-γ) were quantified by flow cytometry. Mouse liver NK cells were isolated from tumor tissue and co-cultured with Hepa1-6-MBL2 or Hepa1-6-vector cells; GZMB, perforin, NK maturation markers (CD27, CD11b), and IFN-γ were assessed by flow cytometry and ELISA. Human NK92 cells were co-cultured with LM3, Hep3B, or Huh7 cells in Transwell systems; NK recruitment was measured by Transwell assay and tumor cell killing by LDH cytotoxicity assay. RGD peptide (integrin β1 blocker) and MK2206 (AKT inhibitor) were used to dissect signaling pathways; si-ITGB1 was used to knockdown integrin β1. Integrin β1 was identified as an MBL2 receptor by immunoprecipitation combined with silver staining and mass spectrometry, confirmed by Co-IP. GST pull-down assays using truncated integrin β1 fragments (ITGB1-ED1 and ITGB1-ED2) determined the binding domain, and surface plasmon resonance measured binding affinity. High-throughput transcriptome sequencing of MBL2-stimulated vs. PBS-treated NK92 cells was followed by pathway enrichment and GSEA analyses. WB was used to assess FAK, PI3K, and AKT phosphorylation in NK cells co-cultured with Hepa1-6-MBL2 cells. ELISA measured GZMB and perforin secretion under MK2206 treatment. A cytokine array profiled cytokines from MBL2-stimulated mouse liver NK cells. Flow cytometry evaluated the effect of selected cytokines (IL-13, IL-25) on CTL proportions and exhaustion markers (PD-1, TIM-3). Jurkat cells were cultured with concentrated NK92 supernatants with or without IL-13 and IL-25 neutralizing antibodies to assess T cell exhaustion reversal. qPCR and WB measured IFNGR1, IFNGR2, IL13R, and IL25R expression in MBL2-overexpressing HCC cells. PD-L1 expression on NK cells was assessed by flow cytometry, qPCR, WB, and immunofluorescence, with RGD and MK2206 inhibitors used to probe pathway dependence. PD-L1 expression in MBL2-modified HCC cell lines was evaluated by WB, and immunofluorescence staining was performed on clinical HCC specimens stratified by MBL2 expression level. HBx-His plasmid was overexpressed in Huh7 cells and MBL2 levels measured by WB and qPCR. RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP) using anti-HBx antibody in 293T cells, followed by PCR and qPCR, was used to demonstrate HBx binding to MBL2 mRNA.

For in vivo experiments, a subcutaneous tumor model in BALB/c nude mice was established using LM3-MBL2, LM3-MBL2ΔSP, or LM3-vector cells; tumor volume and mass were measured, and IHC was performed for Ki67 and NKp46. A subcutaneous HCC model in immunocompetent C57BL/6 mice used Hepa1-6-luc-MBL2 or Hepa1-6-vector cells; NK cells were depleted with anti-ASGM1 antibody and tumor growth monitored; IHC assessed PD-L1 expression. An orthotopic HCC model in C57BL/6 mice used luciferase-labeled Hepa1-6-luc-MBL2 or Hepa1-6-vector cells, with tumor burden quantified by in vivo bioluminescence imaging and NKp46+ NK cell infiltration evaluated by IHC. A second orthotopic model tested the combination of MBL2 overexpression with anti-PD-L1 antibody treatment; IHC assessed NKp46, CD8, and PD-1 expression in tumor tissues. Clinical HCC tissue samples from 10 surgical patients were analyzed by qPCR and WB for MBL2 expression; HCC and normal tissue microarrays were assessed by IHC for MBL2, NKp46, PD-L1, and CD8, and IHC was used to compare MBL2 expression between HBV-positive and HBV-negative HCC specimens.
